title: Equal extended colengths under specialization preserve components
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, locally closed in a smooth finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme; no reducedness is assumed [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For $u\in X$ define $h_{X,u}(n)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,u}/\mathfrak m_u^{n+1})$, $t_u=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(u)$, $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{i=0}^n f(i)$, and $H_X(u)=\Lambda^{t_u}h_{X,u}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length] [def-kun-transcendence-degree] [def-weil-residue-field]. Irreducible components and their dimensions refer to the underlying topological space [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $z,x\in X$ with $x\in\overline{\{z\}}$. If $H_X(z)=H_X(x)$ as sequences, then an irreducible component of $X$ contains $x$ if and only if it contains $z$. In particular the sets $\{\dim Z:x\in Z,\ Z\text{ an irreducible component of }X\}$ and $\{\dim Z:z\in Z,\ Z\text{ an irreducible component of }X\}$ coincide. This concerns actual components through comparable points, not recovery of component dimensions from the Hilbert--Samuel sequence of an arbitrary unrelated local ring.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ is Noetherian (a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal). By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], its components form a finite family. Let $U$ be the complement of the union of those components which do not contain $z$. Thus $z\in U$. The inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc], and is quasi-separated: its diagonal is an isomorphism. Form $Y=\operatorname{SIm}(j)$ with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc], $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent and $|Y|=\overline U$. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open], its restriction to $U$ is the image of the identity of $U$; by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-of-closed-immersion] that image is $U$. Hence $Y|_U=U$ as schemes, so $\mathcal I_z=0$ and $H_Y(z)=H_X(z)$. Also $x\in|Y|$, since $z\in U$ and $x\in\overline{\{z\}}$.

source.place: Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image; properties.tex Tags 01OX and 0BA8. Agent choice of the component-complement open.

proof.text:
The closed subscheme $Y$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Q$: restrict a finite affine finite-type cover of $X$; by [def-weil-closed-immersion] its inverse images have coordinate rings $A/J$, which are generated over $\mathbf Q$ by the images of any generators of $A$. Its locally closed embedding in the given smooth envelope is obtained by adding $J$ to the equations of $X$ on the same open envelope. Thus [lem-per-scheme-hilbert-samuel-test-presentations] applies to $Y$, including its nilpotents. Its closed upper level sets imply
$$H_Y(z)\le_{\mathrm{lex}}H_Y(x).$$
Indeed the closed upper level set for the value $H_Y(z)$ contains $z$, hence its closure and $x$. We use only the semicontinuity assertion of the cited node, not its presentations or blowup assertions.

source.place: Section 6.1, extended function and upper semicontinuity; Section 6.3 and Remark 6.2 motivate the component-profile argument. Agent application to a schematic closure.

proof.text:
Put $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_x$ and $I=\mathcal I_x$. Then $\mathcal O_{Y,x}=R/I$ by the local quotient description of [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The ring $R$ is Noetherian: choose a Noetherian affine chart around $x$ in the locally Noetherian covering supplied in Step 1 and use [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] at the prime of $x$. By [lem-trf-maximal-adic-graded-length-bridge], each $R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ has finite length. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to the surjection
$$R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow R/(I+\mathfrak m^{n+1}).$$
The target is $(R/I)/(\mathfrak m/I)^{n+1}$ and its submodules over $R$ are exactly its submodules over $R/I$, since the action factors through that surjection. Thus $h_{Y,x}(n)\le h_{X,x}(n)$ for every $n$. The residue fields at $x$ coincide. Iterated finite summation preserves pointwise inequalities, so $H_Y(x)\le H_X(x)$ pointwise, hence lexicographically. With Step 2 and the assumed equality this gives
$$H_X(z)=H_Y(z)\le_{\mathrm{lex}}H_Y(x)\le_{\mathrm{lex}}H_X(x)=H_X(z).$$
Consequently $H_Y(x)=H_X(x)$ as sequences.

proof.text:
Finite differences undo summation: for a sequence $f$, $\Lambda f(0)=f(0)$ and $\Lambda f(n+1)-\Lambda f(n)=f(n+1)$. Applying this operation $t_x$ times to Step 3 gives $h_{Y,x}=h_{X,x}$. In the short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow (I+\mathfrak m^{n+1})/\mathfrak m^{n+1}\longrightarrow R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}\longrightarrow R/(I+\mathfrak m^{n+1})\longrightarrow0,$$
[lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] and equality of the finite lengths force the first term to have length zero. A nonzero module has the strict chain $0\subsetneq M$, so has length at least one by [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Hence $I\subseteq\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ for every $n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] with the Noetherian local ring $R$, ideal $\mathfrak m$ (its Jacobson radical), and cyclic finite module $R$. It gives $I\subseteq\bigcap_{n\ge0}\mathfrak m^n=0$. Thus $I=0$.

The equality $\mathcal I_x=0$ gives an open neighbourhood $V$ of $x$ on which $\mathcal I=0$. Explicitly, on a Noetherian affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ at $x$, the quasi-coherent ideal corresponds to an ideal $J\subseteq A$, with finite generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$. If $\mathfrak p$ represents $x$, the equality $J_{\mathfrak p}=0$ supplies $s_i\notin\mathfrak p$ with $s_i a_i=0$. For $s=\prod_i s_i$ (the empty product is $1$), $J_s=0$; take $V=D(s)$. Thus $V\subseteq|Y|=\overline U$. Every component meeting $U$ contains $z$, because $U$ avoids every other component. Therefore $U$ is contained in the union of the components containing $z$. That union is closed since there are finitely many components, so $\overline U$ is contained in it as well.

source.place: Agent finite-generation and localization argument following Tag 01R8; uses the quasi-coherent ideal and finite component family established in Step 1.

proof.text: Let $Z$ be any irreducible component containing $x$. The nonempty open subset $V\cap Z$ is dense in $Z$: otherwise its closure and its closed complement would express $Z$ as a union of two proper closed subsets, contradicting irreducibility. By Step 5, $V\cap Z$ lies in the finite union of components containing $z$, so its closure $Z$ lies in that union. An irreducible set contained in a finite union of closed sets is contained in one of them (apply the definition of irreducibility repeatedly). Maximality of irreducible components forces $Z$ to equal that component. Hence $z\in Z$. Conversely any component containing $z$ is closed and therefore contains $\overline{\{z\}}$, in particular $x$. The component families through $x$ and $z$ are equal, so taking the dimensions of their members gives exactly the asserted equality of sets.
